Analisei a concepção e o estado atual do código (fases 1 a 4 concluídas). Resposta direta: **é tecnicamente possível, mas não é recomendável.** As duas fases não são independentes.

## Por que não são independentes

A fundação já concluída (server.lisp já constrói ambos os apps por `make-app` parametrizado por papel; `render.lisp` já tem os auxiliares `role-*`; `cycle.lisp`/`scheduler.lisp` são os serviços automáticos, comuns e independentes de papel). O acoplamento residual entre as fases 5 e 6 está em três camadas compartilhadas, ainda por construir:

1. **Camada de consulta de oportunidades** (`queries.lisp`). Hoje só há consultas de usuário. Ambas as fases precisam ler oportunidades com os `JOIN` para conta, produto e dimensões. O gerente lê as engajadas do seu time; o agente lê as disponíveis (públicas) e as suas engajadas. A consulta de "oportunidades engajadas com contexto" é largamente comum.

2. **Renderização de lista com filtro e ordenação** (`render.lisp`). A concepção especifica, para os dois papéis, listas com o mesmo maquinário HTMX de filtro (localidade, setor, série, produto, cross-selling, datas) e ordenação. O componente de apresentação de uma oportunidade (campos de contexto, badges de dimensão) é o mesmo; o agente acrescenta controles de ação, o gerente acrescenta colunas de agente, datas, desfecho e justificativa.

3. **Dependência de dados assimétrica.** A aplicação do gerente é essencialmente **somente leitura** — um relatório de acompanhamento sobre os registros de engajamento (desfecho, justificativa, datas) que a aplicação do agente **produz** por escrita. As estruturas que o gerente exibe só se estabilizam na fase 5.

## Recomendação: sequencial, agente primeiro (Fase 5), depois gerente (Fase 6)

- Ambas editariam os mesmos arquivos (`queries.lisp`, `render.lisp`, `handlers.lisp`, rotas em `server.lisp`). Em paralelo, isto gera conflito de merge e divergência de design em vez de reúso;
- A dependência é assimétrica: a fase 6 reaproveita a consulta de leitura, o componente de linha/cartão e o maquinário de filtro/ordenação que a fase 5 estabelece. Construir o agente primeiro permite que o gerente reutilize, não reinvente;
- Sob o escopo MVP, o custo de coordenação do paralelismo real (worktrees separados, integração) não se justifica para duas fases deste porte.

## Se o paralelismo for realmente desejado

O caminho correto **não** é fase-5-contra-fase-6, e sim extrair antes uma sub-tarefa da **substância compartilhada** — consulta de leitura de oportunidades, componente de apresentação da linha e o maquinário de filtro/ordenação — e só então paralelizar "escritas do agente" e "visão do gerente" sobre essa base estável. Isso troca o risco de conflito por um ponto de sincronização explícito, ao custo de uma terceira sub-tarefa e de mais coordenação.

Minha recomendação permanece a sequencial. Deseja que eu prossiga desdobrando a 8W2N nessa ordem (Fase 5 e Fase 6 como subtarefas), ou prefere avaliar a variante com extração da camada compartilhada?

## 1. Spinneret rendering patterns

**HTMX config as static meta, not inline script** (render.lisp:13-18) — this is the key CSP-compatibility trick:
```lisp

  "{\"allowEval\":false,\"includeIndicatorStyles\":false}"
  ...)
```

**`render-head`** (render.lisp:55-65) — common `<head>`: charset, viewport, title, static stylesheet `/assets/app.css`, the `htmx-config` meta, and `<script src="/assets/htmx.min.js" defer>`:
```lisp
(:link :rel "stylesheet" :href "/assets/app.css")
(:meta :name "htmx-config" :content +htmx-config+)
(:script :src "/assets/htmx.min.js" :defer t)
```

**`render-appbar` (role)** (render.lisp:72-78) — minimal top strip for login screens: `header.appbar` > `span.wordmark "LeadScorer"` + `span.scope (role-scope role)`.

**`render-navbar` (role username)** (render.lisp:80-99) — authenticated nav. (:span :class "brand" "LeadScorer"
```lisp
       (when (eq role :manager)
         (spinneret:with-html (:span :class "role" "gerente"))))
...
(:form :class "logout-form" :method "post" :action "/logout"
       (:button :class "btn btn-sm" :type "submit" "Sair"))
```
Note the nested-emit idiom: inside a `with-html` block, a conditional sub-fragment is wrapped in its own `(spinneret:with-html ...)`.

**`render-login-page` (role usernames &optional error-message)** (render.lisp:101-137) — full page string. Shell = `(:doctype)` + `(:html :lang "pt-BR" (render-head …) (:body (render-appbar role) (:main.login-main (:div.card …)) (render-footer)))`. Tokens live in `:root` (app.css:41-56): backgrounds `--bg-base #161616`/`--bg-raised #262626`/`--bg-overlay #393939`; foregrounds `--fg-primary #f4f4f4`/`--fg-secondary`/`--fg-muted`/`--fg-disabled`; status `--positive #42be65`/`--negative #fa4d56`/`--warning #f1c21b`/`--info #4589ff`; spacing scale `--space-1..8` (4→64px); radii `--radius-sm/md`. ---

## 2. The `role-*` helpers (render.lisp:20-53)

All are `(ecase role …)` over `:agent`/`:manager`. Returns:

| fn | `:agent` | `:manager` |
|---|---|---|
| `role-scope` (l.20) | "Aplicação do agente" | "Aplicação do gerente" |
| `role-field-label` (l.26) | "Agente de vendas" | "Gerente de vendas" |
| `role-placeholder` (l.32) | "Escolha um agente" | "Escolha um gerente" |
| `role-context` (l.38) | "agente" | "gerente" |
| `role-hint` (l.44) | "A aplicação do gerente é servida em endereço próprio…" | "A aplicação do agente é servida em endereço próprio…" |

`role-hint` gives the reciprocal note that the *other* app runs at its own address with the same login form, no role management. Pattern to replicate for Phase 5: keep all role-varying copy in `ecase`-per-role pure functions, never branch inline in markup.

---

## 3. The `-for` core-function / dynamic-var testability pattern

**Design statement** (handlers.lisp:5-9): route logic lives in `-for`-suffixed core functions that receive the session table *explicitly* and are therefore testable with no server and no DB (by binding `*list-usernames-fn*` and `*lookup-user-fn*`). The thin Ningle route wrappers in server.lisp only supply the current session table via `session-table`.

**Core functions** (handlers.lisp):
- `html-response (html &optional (status 200))` (l.11) → Clack response `(status (:content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8") <utf-8 octets>)`.
- `redirect (location &optional (status 302))` (l.19) → `(status (:location location) (""))`.
- `login-page-response (role &optional error-message)` (l.23).
- `login-submit-for (role table params)` (l.28) — reads `(cdr (assoc "user" params :test #'string=))`, calls `lookup-user`, on success `session-put` + redirect `/`, else re-render login with error.
- `logout-response-for (table)` (l.42) — `session-clear` + redirect `/login`.
- `home-response-for (role table)` (l.47) — role gate then render home, else redirect `/login`.

**The indirection** (queries.lisp:25-31, 45-52): each DB function has a companion dynamic var defaulting to the DB impl, plus a wrapper that funcalls the var:
```lisp
(defvar *list-usernames-fn* 'db-list-usernames "…Vinculável nos testes…")
(defun list-usernames (role) (funcall *list-usernames-fn* role))

(defvar *lookup-user-fn* 'db-lookup-user "…")
(defun lookup-user (role username) (funcall *lookup-user-fn* role username))
```
The real impls (`db-list-usernames` l.13, `db-lookup-user` l.33) wrap `ls:with-database` + `postmodern:query`, choosing the table by `ecase` on the internal role (never interpolated) and binding external input as `$1`.

**To replicate for opportunity queries in Phase 5:** define `db-<query>` (inside `ls:with-database`, parameterized SQL, `ecase` on role), a `defvar *<query>-fn* '<db-fn>`, and a thin `(<query> …) → (funcall *<query>-fn* …)`. Then write `<action>-for` handlers that take the session `table` explicitly and call the wrappers. Tests rebind the `*…-fn*` vars with lambdas. See handlers test §7 for the exact binding shape.

---

## 4. Session API (session.lisp)

Session keys are keywords; the table is a plain `eq` hash-table placed by Lack's session middleware under `:lack.session`.

- `session-table ()` (l.11) → `(getf (lack/request:request-env ningle:*request*) :lack.session)`. Single point of coupling to Ningle/Lack request env.
- `session-put (table user-id role username)` (l.16) → sets `:user-id`, `:role`, `:username`; returns `table`.
- `session-user (table)` (l.24) → `(values id role username)` or `nil` if no `:user-id`.
- `authenticated-p (table)` (l.31) → `(and table (gethash :user-id table) t)`; nil table ⇒ nil (fail-closed).
- `session-role (table)` (l.36) → `(gethash :role table)`.
- `session-clear (table)` (l.40) → `(clrhash table)`; returns `table`.
- `role-authorized-p (table role)` (l.45) → `(and (authenticated-p table) (eq (session-role table) role))`. This is the per-app authorization gate.

All are pure over the table (no server/DB). Phase 5 agent app should reuse `role-authorized-p`/`session-user` unchanged and store any additional identity (e.g. the resolved agent id) under new keywords via a `session-put`-style setter if needed.

---

## 5. HTMX integration status & CSP

- **No `HX-Request` header inspection exists yet.** Grep of the web tree shows HTMX only in render.lisp (`+htmx-config+`, the script tag) and app.css; handlers/server never read `HX-Request`, `HX-Target`, etc. Partial-swap routing is *not yet implemented* — this is greenfield for Phase 5.
- **HTMX is loaded on every page** as a static, deferred asset with `allowEval:false` and `includeIndicatorStyles:false` (render.lisp:13-18, 64-65). Indicator styles come from app.css instead so `style-src 'self'` holds.
- **Expected partial-swap approach** (implied by the architecture, ADR D2K9 cited in server.lisp:25): same-origin XHR enabled by `connect-src 'self'`; forms/links carry `hx-*` attributes; server returns HTML fragments. To emit fragments, Phase 5 should add helper functions using `spinneret:with-html-string` (fragment, no `:doctype`/`:html`) and branch handlers on the `HX-Request` header (read from `(gethash "hx-request" (getf (lack/request:request-env ningle:*request*) :headers))`, following the `session-table` env-access idiom) to return a partial vs. full page.
- **CSP** (server.lisp:16-25): 
```
default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self';
connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self';
base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```
No `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval`. Consequence for Phase 5: **no inline scripts, no inline styles, no inline event handlers** — all JS via `/assets/*.js`, all styling via classes in app.css, all interactivity via `hx-*` attributes (which are HTML attributes, not inline JS, so they pass). `connect-src 'self'` is what permits HTMX XHR. Applied by `security-headers-middleware` at the top of the stack (server.lisp:27-41), covering assets and error responses too; also adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

---

## 6. Web package exports & ASDF wiring

**`leadscorer/web` package** (package.lisp:3-18): `(:use #:cl)`, local nickname `ls → leadscorer`. Exports only the lifecycle surface:
```
start  stop  start-scheduler  stop-scheduler  scheduler-running-p
make-agent-app  make-manager-app  *agent-app*  *manager-app*
```
Everything else (render/session/queries/handlers) is internal, accessed in tests via `leadscorer/web::` double-colon.

**ASDF** (leadscorer.asd). Four systems. `leadscorer/web` (l.48-63) depends on `"leadscorer" "clack" "clack-handler-hunchentoot" "lack" "lack/middleware/session" "ningle" "spinneret"`, `:serial t`, module `src/web` in load order:
```
package → config → render → session → queries → handlers → scheduler → server
```
Phase 5 files insert into this ordered list; new query/handler files must come after `queries`/`handlers` (or extend them) and before `server` if `server` routes reference them. `leadscorer/web/tests` (l.65-83) depends on `"leadscorer/web" "parachute" "flexi-streams"`, module `tests/web` ordered `main → render → session → queries → handlers → integration → scheduler`, and its `test-op` runs `parachute:test :leadscorer/web/tests`, erroring unless status `:passed`.

---

## 7. Web test conventions

- **Framework:** Parachute. The suite package `leadscorer/web/tests` `(:use #:cl #:parachute)` is defined in tests/web/main.lisp:3-6; every test file does `(in-package #:leadscorer/web/tests)`. Tests use `define-test`, assertions `is`, `true`, `false`, `is eql`, `is equal`, `is =`, and `skip`.
- **`fresh-session` helper** (session.lisp test l.5-7): `(make-hash-table :test 'eq)` — mimics the Lack-provided table. `*sample-usernames*` (render.lisp test l.10-13) is the DB-free username fixture.
- **Binding the `*fns*` in tests** — the exact pattern to copy (handlers.lisp test l.28-37):
```lisp
(let ((table (fresh-session))
      (leadscorer/web::*lookup-user-fn*
        (lambda (role username)
          (if (and (eq role :agent) (string= username "anna.snelling")) 42 nil))))
  (let ((r (leadscorer/web::login-submit-for
            :agent table '(("user" . "anna.snelling")))))
    (is = 302 (response-status r)) ...))
```
Both `*lookup-user-fn*` and `*list-usernames-fn*` are rebound as lambdas in `let` (handlers.lisp test l.42-46; integration.lisp l.52-56). No server, no DB.
- **DB-gated tests** are guarded by `(if (leadscorer::database-reachable-p) … (skip "PostgreSQL indisponível…"))` — see queries.lisp test l.12/31 and scheduler.lisp test l.11/25. The scheduler test additionally gates on `*derived-present-p*` (probe-file of `data/derived/potentials_base.csv`, scheduler.lisp test l.5-8) and TRUNCATEs `opportunity_scores, engagements, opportunities RESTART IDENTITY` (l.17-19) — **these are the opportunity-domain tables Phase 5 will query.** Canonical seed counts: 35 agents, 6 managers (queries.lisp test l.8, 20-21).
- **In-process stack test** (integration.lisp): drives the real middleware+Ningle app without opening ports, via a hand-built Clack env. `make-env (method path &key cookie body)` (l.13-31) constructs the env (headers hash-table, `:raw-body` as `flexi-streams:make-in-memory-input-stream` of UTF-8 octets for POST bodies); `cookie-header-from` (l.33-38) extracts the `name=value` from `Set-Cookie`; `body-string` (l.40-48) decodes octet or string-list bodies. The round-trip test (l.50-96) rebinds both `*…-fn*` vars, then funcalls `(make-agent-app)`/`(make-manager-app)` directly, asserting login markup, static `/assets/app.css` resolution (`text/css`), fail-closed `/`, cookie `lack.session.agent`, authenticated home, logout, and cross-role rejection. **This is the template for Phase 5 integration coverage.**
- Response accessors used across tests: `(defun response-status (r) (first r))` and `(defun response-location (r) (getf (second r) :location))` (handlers.lisp test l.10-11).

---

## Key facts for Phase 5 planning

1. `render-home-page` (render.lisp:139-159) is an explicit placeholder — the dashboard/opportunity lists slot in here.
2. Replicate the `db-X` + `defvar *X-fn*` + wrapper + `X-for(table …)` quartet (queries.lisp + handlers.lisp) for opportunity queries; the opportunity tables are `opportunities`, `engagements`, `opportunity_scores` (scheduler test l.17-19).
3. HTMX partial-swap plumbing does **not** exist yet — no `HX-Request` handling. Add it following the `session-table` env-access idiom, returning `with-html-string` fragments (no doctype).
4. CSP forbids all inline JS/CSS; keep interactivity in `hx-*` attributes and assets under `/assets/`.
5. New source files register in `leadscorer.asd` `src/web` serial list (before `server`); new tests in the `tests/web` serial list; DB tests must `skip` when `(leadscorer::database-reachable-p)` is false.
6. Reuse `role-authorized-p`, `session-user`, `role-*` helpers, `html-response`/`redirect`, and the `role`-driven `ecase` copy convention unchanged.

## 2. The `role-*` helpers (render.lisp:20-53)

All are `(ecase role …)` over `:agent`/`:manager`. Returns:

| fn | `:agent` | `:manager` |
|---|---|---|

## 3. The `-for` core-function / dynamic-var testability pattern

**Design statement** (handlers.lisp:5-9): route logic lives in `-for`-suffixed core functions that receive the session table *explicitly* and are therefore testable with no server and no DB (by binding `*list-usernames-fn*` and `*lookup-user-fn*`). The thin Ningle route wrappers in server.lisp only supply the current session table via `session-table`.

**Core functions** (handlers.lisp):
- `html-response (html &optional (status 200))` (l.11) → Clack response `(status (:content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8") <utf-8 octets>)`.
- `redirect (location &optional (status 302))` (l.19) → `(status (:location location) (""))`.
- `login-page-response (role &optional error-message)` (l.23).
- `login-submit-for (role table params)` (l.28) — reads `(cdr (assoc "user" params :test #'string=))`, calls `lookup-user`, on success `session-put` + redirect `/`, else re-render login with error.
- `logout-response-for (table)` (l.42) — `session-clear` + redirect `/login`.
- `home-response-for (role table)` (l.47) — role gate then render home, else redirect `/login`.

**The indirection** (queries.lisp:25-31, 45-52): each DB function has a companion dynamic var defaulting to the DB impl, plus a wrapper that funcalls the var:
```lisp
(defvar *list-usernames-fn* 'db-list-usernames "…Vinculável nos testes…")
(defun list-usernames (role) (funcall *list-usernames-fn* role))

(defvar *lookup-user-fn* 'db-lookup-user "…")
(defun lookup-user (role username) (funcall *lookup-user-fn* role username))
```
The real impls (`db-list-usernames` l.13, `db-lookup-user` l.33) wrap `ls:with-database` + `postmodern:query`, choosing the table by `ecase` on the internal role (never interpolated) and binding external input as `$1`.

**To replicate for opportunity queries in Phase 5:** define `db-<query>` (inside `ls:with-database`, parameterized SQL, `ecase` on role), a `defvar *<query>-fn* '<db-fn>`, and a thin `(<query> …) → (funcall *<query>-fn* …)`. Then write `<action>-for` handlers that take the session `table` explicitly and call the wrappers. Tests rebind the `*…-fn*` vars with lambdas. See handlers test §7 for the exact binding shape.

## 4. Session API (session.lisp)

Session keys are keywords; the table is a plain `eq` hash-table placed by Lack's session middleware under `:lack.session`.

- `session-table ()` (l.11) → `(getf (lack/request:request-env ningle:*request*) :lack.session)`. Single point of coupling to Ningle/Lack request env.
- `session-put (table user-id role username)` (l.16) → sets `:user-id`, `:role`, `:username`; returns `table`.
- `session-user (table)` (l.24) → `(values id role username)` or `nil` if no `:user-id`.
- `authenticated-p (table)` (l.31) → `(and table (gethash :user-id table) t)`; nil table ⇒ nil (fail-closed).
- `session-role (table)` (l.36) → `(gethash :role table)`.
- `session-clear (table)` (l.40) → `(clrhash table)`; returns `table`.
- `role-authorized-p (table role)` (l.45) → `(and (authenticated-p table) (eq (session-role table) role))`. This is the per-app authorization gate.

All are pure over the table (no server/DB). Phase 5 agent app should reuse `role-authorized-p`/`session-user` unchanged and store any additional identity (e.g. the resolved agent id) under new keywords via a `session-put`-style setter if needed.

## 5. HTMX integration status & CSP

- **No `HX-Request` header inspection exists yet.** Grep of the web tree shows HTMX only in render.lisp (`+htmx-config+`, the script tag) and app.css; handlers/server never read `HX-Request`, `HX-Target`, etc. Partial-swap routing is *not yet implemented* — this is greenfield for Phase 5.
- **HTMX is loaded on every page** as a static, deferred asset with `allowEval:false` and `includeIndicatorStyles:false` (render.lisp:13-18, 64-65). Indicator styles come from app.css instead so `style-src 'self'` holds.
- **Expected partial-swap approach** (implied by the architecture, ADR D2K9 cited in server.lisp:25): same-origin XHR enabled by `connect-src 'self'`; forms/links carry `hx-*` attributes; server returns HTML fragments. To emit fragments, Phase 5 should add helper functions using `spinneret:with-html-string` (fragment, no `:doctype`/`:html`) and branch handlers on the `HX-Request` header (read from `(gethash "hx-request" (getf (lack/request:request-env ningle:*request*) :headers))`, following the `session-table` env-access idiom) to return a partial vs. full page.
- **CSP** (server.lisp:16-25): 
```
default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self';
connect-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; img-src 'self';
base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```
No `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval`. Consequence for Phase 5: **no inline scripts, no inline styles, no inline event handlers** — all JS via `/assets/*.js`, all styling via classes in app.css, all interactivity via `hx-*` attributes (which are HTML attributes, not inline JS, so they pass). `connect-src 'self'` is what permits HTMX XHR. Applied by `security-headers-middleware` at the top of the stack (server.lisp:27-41), covering assets and error responses too; also adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

**`leadscorer/web` package** (package.lisp:3-18): `(:use #:cl)`, local nickname `ls → leadscorer`. Exports only the lifecycle surface:
```
start  stop  start-scheduler  stop-scheduler  scheduler-running-p
make-agent-app  make-manager-app  *agent-app*  *manager-app*
```
Everything else (render/session/queries/handlers) is internal, accessed in tests via `leadscorer/web::` double-colon.

**ASDF** (leadscorer.asd). Four systems. `leadscorer/web` (l.48-63) depends on `"leadscorer" "clack" "clack-handler-hunchentoot" "lack" "lack/middleware/session" "ningle" "spinneret"`, `:serial t`, module `src/web` in load order:

Phase 5 files insert into this ordered list; new query/handler files must come after `queries`/`handlers` (or extend them) and before `server` if `server` routes reference them. `leadscorer/web/tests` (l.65-83) depends on `"leadscorer/web" "parachute" "flexi-streams"`, module `tests/web` ordered `main → render → session → queries → handlers → integration → scheduler`, and its `test-op` runs `parachute:test :leadscorer/web/tests`, erroring unless status `:passed`.

# LeadScorer — Agent Application: UI Structure and Copy Report

Sources: `docs/concepcao-inicial.md`, and prototypes in `.claude/assets/examples/` (`example-home-agente-dark.html`, `example-disponiveis-dark.html`, `example-engajadas-dark.html`, `example-engajar-justificativa-dark.html`, `example-login-agente-dark.html`, `textos-de-ajuda.md`). The prototypes are explicitly non-normative ("protótipo estático não normativo"); the design system (`.claude/rules/design.md` + `.claude/assets/tokens/`) is the canonical style source. Copy below is quoted verbatim from the prototypes.

## Domain model recap (concepcao-inicial.md, "Oportunidade e ciclo de engajamento", "Modelo de qualificação", "Ciclo de computação")

- An opportunity is an account-product pair. Two persistent states: `prospecting` (public, available to all agents) and `engaging` (pulled by one agent, visible only to that agent). Outcomes `won`/`lost` are NOT persistent states — they are events in the engagement-cycle history; the opportunity returns to `prospecting` after outcome, with decayed potential.
- An agent may hold up to **ten** simultaneous engagements (arbitrary limit).
- The first ten displayed opportunities are the agent's **top tier**. Engaging outside the top tier requires a justification: (a) discordância da avaliação; (b) consulta direta do cliente; (c) outro motivo.
- Potential is an integer 0–100 over six dimensions. Four are active (weighted); two are inert (weight zero, not shown as columns). Aggregation is a non-compensatory eligibility gate + weighted geometric mean of the four active dimensions (not a weighted sum); low momentum drags the index, null momentum zeroes it (ADR C4X9).
- Accelerated MVP cycle (`Ciclo de computação`): ranking service every minute; decay/expiration service every minute; an engaged opportunity **expires in twenty minutes**. Ranking is recomputed per (available-pair × agent).

---

## 1. Tela inicial (home) of the agent — `example-home-agente-dark.html`

Page head: `<h1>Meu desempenho</h1>` with sub `agente anna-snelling --- acumulado`.

Per concepcao-inicial.md ("Faixa de indicadores"), derived by aggregation over `engagements` history. Card copy exactly as in the prototype (label / value / foot):

| # | Label | Value (sample) | Foot | Meaning (spec) |
|---|-------|-------|------|------|
| 1 | `Engajamentos` | `34` | `ciclos acumulados` | Total accumulated engagement cycles |
| 2 | `Sucessos` (card `.kpi.pos`, value `.pos`) | `21` | `desfecho won` | Count of `won` cycles |
| 3 | `Taxa de sucesso` | `61,8` + unit `%` | `won sobre fechados` | won / (won+lost), percentage points |
| 4 | `Ticket médio` | unit `US$ ` + `2.847` | `média de fechamento` | Mean close value of `won`, USD |
| 5 | `Total em vendas` (card `.kpi.pos`, value `.pos`) | unit `US$ ` + `59.787` | `soma dos won` | Sum of close value of `won`, USD |
| 6 | `Tempo médio de venda` | `47` + unit ` d` | `engajamento a fechamento` | Mean days engagement→close of `won` |

## 3. Engajamento flow — `example-engajar-justificativa-dark.html`

The `Engajar` button appears per-row on disponíveis and home. Two interaction states are prototyped.

Page intro copy: `Dois estados da interação de engajamento a partir da lista de disponíveis... O engajamento dentro do top tier é direto; fora dele exige justificativa; e é bloqueado quando o limite de dez oportunidades simultâneas já foi atingido.`

### State 1 — Justification modal (only outside top tier)
Stage label: `Estado 1 --- Engajamento fora do top tier: justificativa obrigatória`.
Modal (`.modal`, `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`):
- Title `<h2>Justificar engajamento</h2>`
- Context line: `A oportunidade <b>Dalttechnology --- GTX Basic</b> (potencial 57) está na posição 12, fora do seu top tier. Registre o motivo do desvio da recomendação do modelo.`
- Legend: `Motivo do engajamento`
- Three radio options (`name="just"`), each with title `.t` + description `.d`:
  1. `Discordância da avaliação` — `Julgo o potencial desta oportunidade maior do que o atribuído.` (checked by default)
  2. `Consulta direta do cliente` — `O cliente procurou diretamente sobre este produto.`
  3. `Outro motivo` — `Motivo diverso dos anteriores.`
- Actions: `Cancelar` (`.btn`), `Confirmar engajamento` (`.btn.btn-primary`)
- Foot note: `Engajamentos dentro do top tier não exigem justificativa.`

The modal appears ONLY when engaging an opportunity outside the top tier (positions 11+). Top-tier engagement is direct (no modal). These map to the three seeded `engagement_justifications` (justification_id is null for top-tier engagements).

### State 2 — Ten-engagement limit block
Stage label: `Estado 2 --- Limite de dez oportunidades atingido: bloqueio`.
Alert modal (`.modal.alert`, `role="alertdialog"`):
- Mark badge (warning): `Limite atingido`
- Title `<h2>Carteira de engajamento cheia</h2>`
- Body: `Você já possui <b>dez</b> oportunidades engajadas, o limite de engajamentos simultâneos. Conclua uma venda (won ou lost) ou devolva uma oportunidade para engajar outra.`

# LeadScorer — Agent Application: UI Structure and Copy Report

Sources: `docs/concepcao-inicial.md`, and prototypes in `.claude/assets/examples/` (`example-home-agente-dark.html`, `example-disponiveis-dark.html`, `example-engajadas-dark.html`, `example-engajar-justificativa-dark.html`, `example-login-agente-dark.html`, `textos-de-ajuda.md`). The prototypes are explicitly non-normative ("protótipo estático não normativo"); the design system (`.claude/rules/design.md` + `.claude/assets/tokens/`) is the canonical style source. Copy below is quoted verbatim from the prototypes.

## Domain model recap (concepcao-inicial.md, "Oportunidade e ciclo de engajamento", "Modelo de qualificação", "Ciclo de computação")

- An opportunity is an account-product pair. Two persistent states: `prospecting` (public, available to all agents) and `engaging` (pulled by one agent, visible only to that agent). Outcomes `won`/`lost` are NOT persistent states — they are events in the engagement-cycle history; the opportunity returns to `prospecting` after outcome, with decayed potential.
- An agent may hold up to **ten** simultaneous engagements (arbitrary limit).
- The first ten displayed opportunities are the agent's **top tier**. Engaging outside the top tier requires a justification: (a) discordância da avaliação; (b) consulta direta do cliente; (c) outro motivo.
- Potential is an integer 0–100 over six dimensions. Four are active (weighted); two are inert (weight zero, not shown as columns). Aggregation is a non-compensatory eligibility gate + weighted geometric mean of the four active dimensions (not a weighted sum); low momentum drags the index, null momentum zeroes it (ADR C4X9).
- Accelerated MVP cycle (`Ciclo de computação`): ranking service every minute; decay/expiration service every minute; an engaged opportunity **expires in twenty minutes**. Ranking is recomputed per (available-pair × agent).

## E. The virtual clock (answer to Q5)

Full chain in `cycle.lisp`:

- `clock-now` (`:46-48`) = `(funcall *clock-fn*)`, default `*clock-fn* = 'now-unix-ms` (`:38-40`). `now-unix-ms` (`db.lisp:87-90`) = real UNIX-ms, second resolution.
- `*virtual-t0*` (`:42-44`) = real UNIX-ms captured at scheduler start. Set exactly once in `start-scheduler`: `(setf ls:*virtual-t0* (ls:now-unix-ms))` (`scheduler.lisp:49`). Exported.
- `decay-horizon-days(model)` (`:50-53`) = `(1- (length (model-decay model)))`.
- `clock-compression(horizon-days)` (`:55-59`) = exact rational `(horizon-days * +ms-per-day+) / (expiration-ms)`; `expiration-ms` = `*expiration-minutes* * 60000` (`config.lisp:162-164`). 20 real minutes ≈ the full virtual horizon.
- `virtual-now(real-now t0 epoch horizon-days)` (`:61-64`, pure) = `epoch + round((real-now − t0) * compression)`.
- **`current-virtual-now(model)` (`:66-69`)** = `(virtual-now (clock-now) *virtual-t0* *virtual-epoch* (decay-horizon-days model))`.

**So an interactive engage/close handler must stamp `engaged_at`/`closed_at` = `(current-virtual-now model)`**, NOT `now-unix-ms`. The cycle.lisp header (`:12-20`) states this contract explicitly: a raw real (~2026) instant would sit far above virtual-now (~2017), giving negative→clamped-0 age, so the opportunity would never decay or expire.

**Dependencies the handler needs but that are not yet exported:** `current-virtual-now`, `*virtual-epoch*`, `decay-horizon-days`/`model-decay`, and a `model` instance. The scheduler already holds one at `leadscorer/web::*scheduler-model*` (`scheduler.lisp:18-19,50-51`) — Phase 5 can reuse it, but it is currently a `defvar` inside the web package (not exported). `run-cycle-tick`/`rank`/`decay`/`expire` default their `:now` to `(current-virtual-now model)` (`cycle.lisp:201,226,274,304`), confirming the intended call.

## F. Answers to the specific questions

### Q1 — List "prospecting" opportunities for an agent with overall + 4 sub-scores + context

`opportunity_scores` already holds per-agent, per-dimension rows (written by the ranking driver for every prospecting opp × every agent — `rank-prospecting-opportunities`, `cycle.lisp:226-272`). A Phase-5 query, given `$1 = agent-id`, would be:

```sql
SELECT o.id,
       a.name AS account, a.sector, a.location, a.employees,
       a.revenue_amount, a.revenue_currency, a.year_established,
       p.name AS product, p.series,
       s.score_overall, s.score_economic, s.score_affinity,
       s.score_momentum, s.score_adherence,
       s.score_closing_time, s.score_inactivity, s.computed_at
FROM opportunities o
JOIN accounts  a ON a.id = o.account_id
JOIN products  p ON p.id = o.product_id
JOIN opportunity_scores s
     ON s.opportunity_id = o.id AND s.sales_agent_id = $1
WHERE o.status = 'prospecting'
ORDER BY s.score_overall DESC;
```

The exact join shape already exists in `rank-prospecting-opportunities` (`cycle.lisp:243-248`, joins accounts+products) and `decay-engaged-opportunities` (`:281-288`). Postmodern binding style is positional `$1,$2,…` with `postmodern:query`/`postmodern:execute` and result modifiers `:single` / `:column` / row-lists (see `db.lisp`, `queries.lisp:19-43`). No named/keyword parameter binding — always positional.

The top-tier cut for the UI is the first `*top-tier-size*`=10 rows of that ordering (justification required to engage beyond it — see Q3).

### Q2 — Lifecycle states & where stored

Only **two** states, stored in `opportunities.status`: `'prospecting'` and `'engaging'` (CHECK-constrained, `0002:16`). There is no separate "won/lost/returned" opportunity state — outcomes live on the **`engagements`** history rows (`outcome`, `closed_at`, `expired`). An opportunity is the account-product pair with a single active state; each engage/close is one `engagements` row. Invariants (enforced by `verify.lisp:46-69`): a `prospecting` opp has NO open engagement (`closed_at IS NULL`); an `engaging` opp has exactly one open engagement whose `sales_agent_id = engaged_by_id`.

### Q3 — To ENGAGE (writes needed)

There is **no existing interactive engage helper** — only the batch seed writers (`seed-opportunities`/`seed-engagements`, `seed.lisp:251-320`) and the expiration path. Phase 5 must, inside one `postmodern:with-transaction`:

1. **Insert an `engagements` row**: `opportunity_id`, `sales_agent_id`, `engaged_at = (current-virtual-now model)`, `justification_id` (nullable — required only when engaging outside the agent's top-tier of `*top-tier-size*`), `closed_at`/`outcome`/`close_value_*` left NULL, `expired` default FALSE. Pattern to mirror: `seed.lisp:303-320`.
2. **Flip the opportunity**: `UPDATE opportunities SET status='engaging', engaged_by_id=$agent, engaged_at=$virtual-now WHERE id=$opp AND status='prospecting'` — must set all three together to satisfy `opportunities_active_state`.

**Business guards to add** (defaults exist but are not yet enforced anywhere in code): `*max-engagements*`=10 — count `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM opportunities WHERE engaged_by_id=$agent AND status='engaging'` and reject at 10. Justification (`engagement_justifications`, seeded codes `disagreement` / `direct-inquiry` / `other`, `seed.lisp:191-203`) is the "justificativa fora do top tier" per the spec.

Existing `engagements` columns to write on engage: `engaged_at` (required), `justification_id` (optional). On close you additionally use `closed_at`, `outcome`, `close_value_amount`, `close_value_currency`, `expired`.

### Q4 — Close (won/lost) or return without outcome

Model the existing expiration path (`expire-due-opportunities`, `cycle.lisp:201-224`) which is the only close writer today. For an interactive close, in one transaction:

- **Won/Lost**: `UPDATE engagements SET closed_at=$virtual-now, outcome='won'|'lost', close_value_amount=$cents, close_value_currency=$ccy WHERE opportunity_id=$opp AND closed_at IS NULL`. Then `UPDATE opportunities SET status='prospecting', engaged_by_id=NULL, engaged_at=NULL WHERE id=$opp`. Invariant: any row with `outcome IS NOT NULL` must have `close_value_amount` (verify.lisp:67-69) — so a Won/Lost must carry a close value (expiration writes amount 0 + house currency `*seed-currency*` for lost, `cycle.lisp:213-219`).
- **Return without outcome**: `UPDATE engagements SET closed_at=$virtual-now WHERE opportunity_id=$opp AND closed_at IS NULL` with `outcome` left NULL, no close value (allowed by schema and by the `outcome IS NOT NULL` invariant). Then same `opportunities` flip back to `prospecting`. This closes the cycle so the "engaging has open cycle" invariant holds.

**Reconciliation afterward (automatic, next scheduler tick — `run-cycle-tick`, `cycle.lisp:304-313`):**
- `rank-prospecting-opportunities` DELETEs `opportunity_scores` for non-prospecting opps, then re-upserts scores for the now-prospecting opp for every agent (`:256-271`). It reads the latest live close via `SELECT opportunity_id, MAX(closed_at) … closed_at > *virtual-epoch* GROUP BY` (`:249-255`) and feeds it to `score-prospecting` (`:130-154`), so a just-closed/returned pair re-enters with a **decayed-then-recovering** momentum via the maturity hump (`momentum-maturity`, `scoring.lisp:108-120`) rather than its static score.
- `decay-engaged-opportunities` (`:274-302`) only touches still-`engaging` opps.
- `expire-due-opportunities` closes any `engaging` opp whose virtual age ≥ horizon as `lost`+`expired=TRUE` and returns it to prospecting (`:201-224`).

Because reconciliation is tick-driven (default 60 s, `*ranking-interval-seconds*`), the UI won't see fresh `opportunity_scores` for a returned opp until the next tick unless Phase 5 also recomputes inline.

### Q5 — Virtual-now for the engage handler

Covered fully in section E. The one line the handler needs: `(ls:current-virtual-now model)` where `model` is a loaded/held `model` struct and `ls:*virtual-t0*` was set at scheduler start. Both `current-virtual-now` and a shared `model` handle must be surfaced to `leadscorer/web` (neither is exported today).

# LeadScorer — Data & Cycle Layer Report (for Phase 5 planning)

## A. Package / export surface (important constraint)

`src/package.lisp` — the `#:leadscorer` package exports only a subset. **Exported and usable from `leadscorer/web`:** `with-database`, `now-unix-ms`, `run-cycle-tick`, `ranking-interval-ms`, `load-model`, `model-agents`, `*virtual-t0*`, and the `scored-*` accessors.

**NOT exported (Phase 5 will need to export these or add wrappers):** `current-virtual-now`, `virtual-now`, `decay-horizon-days`, `*virtual-epoch*`, `model-decay`, `upsert-score`, `expire-due-opportunities`, `rank-prospecting-opportunities`, `*max-engagements*`, `*top-tier-size*`. See `src/package.lisp:6-34`.

The web package (`src/web/package.lisp`) uses local nickname `ls` for `leadscorer` and currently exposes only server/scheduler lifecycle + app builders.

---

## B. DB schema — exact columns

### Reference group — `db/migrations/0001_reference.sql`

**`sales_agents`** (`:25-30`): `id SERIAL PK`, `name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, `username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, `sales_manager_id INTEGER NOT NULL → sales_managers`.

**`accounts`** (`:32-42`) — this is the client-context table: `id`, `name TEXT UNIQUE`, `sector TEXT NOT NULL`, `year_established INTEGER` (nullable), `revenue_amount BIGINT NOT NULL`, `revenue_currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL`, `employees INTEGER` (nullable — the "size" field), `location TEXT` (nullable — locality), `subsidiary_of_id INTEGER → accounts` (self-FK).

**`products`** (`:44-50`): `id`, `name TEXT UNIQUE`, `series TEXT NOT NULL`, `list_price_amount INTEGER NOT NULL`, `list_price_currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL`.

**`engagement_justifications`** (`:52-56`): `id`, `code TEXT UNIQUE`, `description TEXT NOT NULL`. Seeded with 3 rows (see below).

Also `regional_offices`, `sales_managers` (`:13-23`).

> Note on your requested join fields: **founding date** is only `accounts.year_established` (a year, not a date). **client size** = `accounts.employees`. **locality** = `accounts.location`. **revenue** = `revenue_amount`/`revenue_currency`. **product series/name** = `products.series`/`products.name`. **Cross-selling indicator, average decision term (cadence), and last purchase value are NOT columns in any DB table** — they live only in the CSV-derived model (`pair` struct: `last-close-value`, `cadence-days`, `series`; `model.lisp:32-46`). If Phase 5 must display them, they come from `load-model`, not SQL.

### Engagement-cycle group — `db/migrations/0002_engagement_cycle.sql`

**`opportunities`** (`:12-29`): `id SERIAL PK`, `account_id → accounts`, `product_id → products`, `status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('prospecting','engaging'))`, `engaged_by_id INTEGER → sales_agents` (nullable), `engaged_at BIGINT` (nullable, UNIX-ms), `created_at BIGINT NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE (account_id, product_id)`.
Critical CHECK constraint `opportunities_active_state` (`:23-28`): `engaging` ⇒ both `engaged_by_id` and `engaged_at` NOT NULL; `prospecting` ⇒ both NULL. **Any engage/close write must satisfy this atomically.**

**`opportunity_scores`** (`:31-45`): `id SERIAL PK`, `opportunity_id → opportunities`, `sales_agent_id → sales_agents`, `score_overall INTEGER NOT NULL (0..100)`, `score_economic`, `score_affinity`, `score_momentum`, `score_adherence` (all NOT NULL 0..100), `score_closing_time INTEGER (0..100, NULLABLE)`, `score_inactivity INTEGER (0..100, NULLABLE)`, `computed_at BIGINT NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE (opportunity_id, sales_agent_id)`.
→ **It stores per-dimension values, not just an overall.** Four active dimensions are the NOT-NULL columns; the two inert ones are the nullable columns.

**`engagements`** (`:47-67`): `id SERIAL PK`, `opportunity_id → opportunities`, `sales_agent_id → sales_agents`, `justification_id INTEGER → engagement_justifications` (nullable), `engaged_at BIGINT NOT NULL`, `closed_at BIGINT` (nullable), `outcome TEXT CHECK (outcome IN ('won','lost'))` (nullable), `expired BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`, `close_value_amount INTEGER` (nullable), `close_value_currency CHAR(3)` (nullable), `source_opportunity_id TEXT` (provenance only).
CHECK `engagements_close_currency` (`:63-66`): amount and currency are both-null or both-present.

**Dimension name mapping** (your PT labels → columns): Momentum → `score_momentum`; Retorno → `score_economic`; Afinidade → `score_affinity`; Persuasão → `score_adherence` (agent adherence). Inert: Diligência → `score_closing_time`; Atividade → `score_inactivity`. Confirmed by `upsert-score` writing exactly the 4 active columns and leaving the 2 inert null (`cycle.lisp:175-197`, comment at `:176-178`; migration comment `0002:40`).

---

## C. Score struct & composite (scoring.lisp / model.lisp)

`scored` struct — `scoring.lisp:40-50`: fields `agent account product` (strings), `economic affinity adherence` (0-100 reals), `momentum` (0-1 real), `composite` (0-100). Accessors `scored-economic/affinity/adherence/momentum/composite` are all exported.

Composite/overall production — `composite` (`scoring.lisp:156-162`) dispatches on `*composite-form*`; default `:geometric` → `geometric-composite` (`:138-154`): weighted geometric mean of the four dimensions (momentum rescaled ×100), base dims floored at `*dimension-floor*`=1.0, momentum=0 ⇒ composite 0. Weights: economic 0.40, affinity 0.35, adherence 0.25, momentum 0.5 (exponent) — `:14-31`.

`upsert-score` (`cycle.lisp:175-197`) converts to ints via `score->int` (clamp 0-100, `:169-171`); note `score_momentum` is stored as `(round (* 100 momentum))`.

Per-dimension model accessors used to build the four dims: `score-triple` (`scoring.lisp:204-219`) normalizes economic against `model-economic-values`, affinity against `model-affinities`, adherence against `model-adherence-values`, then `composite`.

---

## D. Config values (exact names & read path)

`src/config.lisp` defparameters (compiled fallbacks): `*max-engagements*`=10 (`:15`), `*top-tier-size*`=10 (`:18`), `*expiration-minutes*`=20 (`:21`), `*ranking-interval-seconds*`=60 (`:25`), `*virtual-epoch*`=1514678400000 = 2017-12-31Z (`:34-37`), `+ms-per-day+`=86400000 constant (`:43`).

Canonical source is `config/model.lisp` (a single s-expression read as data with `*read-eval*` nil, symbols interned as keywords) — `config.lisp:86-158`. It sets `:max-engagements 10`, `:top-tier-size 10`, `:expiration-minutes 20`, `:virtual-epoch 1514678400000`, plus scoring weights (`config/model.lisp:13-33`). `load-config` (`config.lisp:146-158`) validates against `*config-schema*` (`:64-82`) and applies via `apply-config-entry` (`:118-137`). Decay params are **data-driven** from `decay.csv` (the `model-decay` vector), NOT a config key (see `config/model.lisp:30-32`); horizon = vector length − 1.

The scheduler calls `ls:load-config` at start (`scheduler.lisp:48`).

---

## E. The virtual clock (answer to Q5)

Full chain in `cycle.lisp`:

- `clock-now` (`:46-48`) = `(funcall *clock-fn*)`, default `*clock-fn* = 'now-unix-ms` (`:38-40`). `now-unix-ms` (`db.lisp:87-90`) = real UNIX-ms, second resolution.
- `*virtual-t0*` (`:42-44`) = real UNIX-ms captured at scheduler start. Set exactly once in `start-scheduler`: `(setf ls:*virtual-t0* (ls:now-unix-ms))` (`scheduler.lisp:49`). Exported.
- `decay-horizon-days(model)` (`:50-53`) = `(1- (length (model-decay model)))`.
- `clock-compression(horizon-days)` (`:55-59`) = exact rational `(horizon-days * +ms-per-day+) / (expiration-ms)`; `expiration-ms` = `*expiration-minutes* * 60000` (`config.lisp:162-164`). 20 real minutes ≈ the full virtual horizon.
- `virtual-now(real-now t0 epoch horizon-days)` (`:61-64`, pure) = `epoch + round((real-now − t0) * compression)`.
- **`current-virtual-now(model)` (`:66-69`)** = `(virtual-now (clock-now) *virtual-t0* *virtual-epoch* (decay-horizon-days model))`.

**So an interactive engage/close handler must stamp `engaged_at`/`closed_at` = `(current-virtual-now model)`**, NOT `now-unix-ms`. The cycle.lisp header (`:12-20`) states this contract explicitly: a raw real (~2026) instant would sit far above virtual-now (~2017), giving negative→clamped-0 age, so the opportunity would never decay or expire.

**Dependencies the handler needs but that are not yet exported:** `current-virtual-now`, `*virtual-epoch*`, `decay-horizon-days`/`model-decay`, and a `model` instance. The scheduler already holds one at `leadscorer/web::*scheduler-model*` (`scheduler.lisp:18-19,50-51`) — Phase 5 can reuse it, but it is currently a `defvar` inside the web package (not exported). `run-cycle-tick`/`rank`/`decay`/`expire` default their `:now` to `(current-virtual-now model)` (`cycle.lisp:201,226,274,304`), confirming the intended call.

---

## F. Answers to the specific questions

### Q1 — List "prospecting" opportunities for an agent with overall + 4 sub-scores + context

`opportunity_scores` already holds per-agent, per-dimension rows (written by the ranking driver for every prospecting opp × every agent — `rank-prospecting-opportunities`, `cycle.lisp:226-272`). A Phase-5 query, given `$1 = agent-id`, would be:

```sql
SELECT o.id,
       a.name AS account, a.sector, a.location, a.employees,
       a.revenue_amount, a.revenue_currency, a.year_established,
       p.name AS product, p.series,
       s.score_overall, s.score_economic, s.score_affinity,
       s.score_momentum, s.score_adherence,
       s.score_closing_time, s.score_inactivity, s.computed_at
FROM opportunities o
JOIN accounts  a ON a.id = o.account_id
JOIN products  p ON p.id = o.product_id
JOIN opportunity_scores s
     ON s.opportunity_id = o.id AND s.sales_agent_id = $1
WHERE o.status = 'prospecting'
ORDER BY s.score_overall DESC;
```

The exact join shape already exists in `rank-prospecting-opportunities` (`cycle.lisp:243-248`, joins accounts+products) and `decay-engaged-opportunities` (`:281-288`). Postmodern binding style is positional `$1,$2,…` with `postmodern:query`/`postmodern:execute` and result modifiers `:single` / `:column` / row-lists (see `db.lisp`, `queries.lisp:19-43`). No named/keyword parameter binding — always positional.

The top-tier cut for the UI is the first `*top-tier-size*`=10 rows of that ordering (justification required to engage beyond it — see Q3).

### Q2 — Lifecycle states & where stored

Only **two** states, stored in `opportunities.status`: `'prospecting'` and `'engaging'` (CHECK-constrained, `0002:16`). There is no separate "won/lost/returned" opportunity state — outcomes live on the **`engagements`** history rows (`outcome`, `closed_at`, `expired`). An opportunity is the account-product pair with a single active state; each engage/close is one `engagements` row. Invariants (enforced by `verify.lisp:46-69`): a `prospecting` opp has NO open engagement (`closed_at IS NULL`); an `engaging` opp has exactly one open engagement whose `sales_agent_id = engaged_by_id`.

### Q3 — To ENGAGE (writes needed)

There is **no existing interactive engage helper** — only the batch seed writers (`seed-opportunities`/`seed-engagements`, `seed.lisp:251-320`) and the expiration path. Phase 5 must, inside one `postmodern:with-transaction`:

1. **Insert an `engagements` row**: `opportunity_id`, `sales_agent_id`, `engaged_at = (current-virtual-now model)`, `justification_id` (nullable — required only when engaging outside the agent's top-tier of `*top-tier-size*`), `closed_at`/`outcome`/`close_value_*` left NULL, `expired` default FALSE. Pattern to mirror: `seed.lisp:303-320`.
2. **Flip the opportunity**: `UPDATE opportunities SET status='engaging', engaged_by_id=$agent, engaged_at=$virtual-now WHERE id=$opp AND status='prospecting'` — must set all three together to satisfy `opportunities_active_state`.

**Business guards to add** (defaults exist but are not yet enforced anywhere in code): `*max-engagements*`=10 — count `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM opportunities WHERE engaged_by_id=$agent AND status='engaging'` and reject at 10. Justification (`engagement_justifications`, seeded codes `disagreement` / `direct-inquiry` / `other`, `seed.lisp:191-203`) is the "justificativa fora do top tier" per the spec.

Existing `engagements` columns to write on engage: `engaged_at` (required), `justification_id` (optional). On close you additionally use `closed_at`, `outcome`, `close_value_amount`, `close_value_currency`, `expired`.

### Q4 — Close (won/lost) or return without outcome

Model the existing expiration path (`expire-due-opportunities`, `cycle.lisp:201-224`) which is the only close writer today. For an interactive close, in one transaction:

- **Won/Lost**: `UPDATE engagements SET closed_at=$virtual-now, outcome='won'|'lost', close_value_amount=$cents, close_value_currency=$ccy WHERE opportunity_id=$opp AND closed_at IS NULL`. Then `UPDATE opportunities SET status='prospecting', engaged_by_id=NULL, engaged_at=NULL WHERE id=$opp`. Invariant: any row with `outcome IS NOT NULL` must have `close_value_amount` (verify.lisp:67-69) — so a Won/Lost must carry a close value (expiration writes amount 0 + house currency `*seed-currency*` for lost, `cycle.lisp:213-219`).
- **Return without outcome**: `UPDATE engagements SET closed_at=$virtual-now WHERE opportunity_id=$opp AND closed_at IS NULL` with `outcome` left NULL, no close value (allowed by schema and by the `outcome IS NOT NULL` invariant). Then same `opportunities` flip back to `prospecting`. This closes the cycle so the "engaging has open cycle" invariant holds.

**Reconciliation afterward (automatic, next scheduler tick — `run-cycle-tick`, `cycle.lisp:304-313`):**
- `rank-prospecting-opportunities` DELETEs `opportunity_scores` for non-prospecting opps, then re-upserts scores for the now-prospecting opp for every agent (`:256-271`). It reads the latest live close via `SELECT opportunity_id, MAX(closed_at) … closed_at > *virtual-epoch* GROUP BY` (`:249-255`) and feeds it to `score-prospecting` (`:130-154`), so a just-closed/returned pair re-enters with a **decayed-then-recovering** momentum via the maturity hump (`momentum-maturity`, `scoring.lisp:108-120`) rather than its static score.
- `decay-engaged-opportunities` (`:274-302`) only touches still-`engaging` opps.
- `expire-due-opportunities` closes any `engaging` opp whose virtual age ≥ horizon as `lost`+`expired=TRUE` and returns it to prospecting (`:201-224`).

Because reconciliation is tick-driven (default 60 s, `*ranking-interval-seconds*`), the UI won't see fresh `opportunity_scores` for a returned opp until the next tick unless Phase 5 also recomputes inline.

### Q5 — Virtual-now for the engage handler

Covered fully in section E. The one line the handler needs: `(ls:current-virtual-now model)` where `model` is a loaded/held `model` struct and `ls:*virtual-t0*` was set at scheduler start. Both `current-virtual-now` and a shared `model` handle must be surfaced to `leadscorer/web` (neither is exported today).

---

## G. Gaps Phase 5 must close (summary)

1. Export from `leadscorer`: `current-virtual-now` (+ `*virtual-epoch*`, `decay-horizon-days`/`model-decay`), and either export `upsert-score` or add a public engage/close service.
2. Provide a shared `model` to request handlers (reuse `*scheduler-model*` or `load-model` per request).
3. Write the interactive engage/close/return DB services (none exist; only seed + expiration writers). Enforce `*max-engagements*`=10 and top-tier justification (`*top-tier-size*`=10) — currently unenforced in code.
4. Web read queries + render for the opportunity list, per-agent scores, and dimension breakdown (only login/home render exists today — `render.lisp:139-159` home is a placeholder).
5. All engage/close writes must be single transactions honoring `opportunities_active_state` and the `engagements` outcome/close-value invariants, stamping virtual time.

Key files: `src/cycle.lisp`, `src/scoring.lisp`, `src/model.lisp`, `src/config.lisp`, `config/model.lisp`, `src/db.lisp`, `db/migrations/0001_reference.sql`, `db/migrations/0002_engagement_cycle.sql`, `src/seed.lisp` (write patterns), `src/verify.lisp` (invariants), and the `src/web/` layer (scaffolded: server, scheduler, session, queries, render — no opportunity features yet).</result>

# Plano --- P3W7: Aplicacao do agente (Fase 5 de 8W2N)

## Contexto

A tarefa-pai 8W2N (interface web) tem as fases 1 a 4 concluidas: prototipagem estatica
(V7C2), esqueleto e sessao (K9X4) e servicos de ciclo (R7M4). Esta subtarefa (P3W7)
constroi a primeira das duas aplicacoes de negocio, a do agente de vendas, sobre a
fundacao `leadscorer/web` existente. Ela e o ponto de contato do usuario final e produz
por escrita os registros de engajamento que a aplicacao do gerente (Fase 6) le. Sem ela,

  achados; verificacoes de HTML/CSS pertinentes.
- Conducao ao vivo: subir `leadscorer/web:start`; via navegador (Claude-in-Chrome no
  viewport do iPhone 13) ou `curl`, logar como agente semeado, abrir Disponiveis (checar
  top tier, corte, filtros/ordenacao por query), engajar uma do top tier (direto) e uma
  fora (modal de justificativa), atingir o limite de dez (alerta), abrir Engajadas, aplicar
  Won/Lost/Devolver, e confirmar as invariantes com `verify.lisp` (ciclo aberto/fechado,
  valor de fechamento, faixa de scores). Reseed ao estado limpo apos a conducao.

3. Auxiliares puros de apresentacao (`view.lisp`).
4. Renderizacao das paginas e fragmentos.
5. Handlers, rotas e deteccao HX; teste de integracao do fluxo.
6. Porte do CSS; validacao responsiva (viewport iPhone 13).
7. Verificacao completa e condução ponta a ponta.

Cada passo e uma fronteira de commit.

## Arquivos criticos

- Editar: `config/model.lisp`, `src/config.lisp`, `src/package.lisp`,
  `src/web/queries.lisp`, `src/web/render.lisp`, `src/web/handlers.lisp`,
  `src/web/server.lisp`, `src/web/static/app.css`, `leadscorer.asd`.
- Novos: `src/engagement.lisp`, `src/web/model-context.lisp`, `src/web/view.lisp`,
  e os arquivos de teste correspondentes sob `tests/` e `tests/web/`.
- Reuso direto: `role-authorized-p`/`session-user` (`session.lisp:24,45`), `role-*` e
  `render-head/navbar/footer` (`render.lisp:20-99`), `html-response`/`redirect`
  (`handlers.lisp:11,19`), `current-virtual-now` e o JOIN de contexto (`cycle.lisp:66-69,
  243-248`), `scored-*`/`score-triple` (`scoring.lisp`), `with-database`/`with-transaction`
  (`db.lisp`), padrao de escrita de `seed.lisp:303-320`, invariantes de `verify.lisp:46-69`.

## Riscos e ressalvas

- CSP proibe estilo/JS inline: barras por classes quantizadas; modal dispensado de ESC/
  clique-no-backdrop no MVP (dismiss so pelo botao Cancelar via troca HTMX), sem JS proprio.
- Acoplamento web<->modelo por nome (conta, produto) para os dois campos do modelo; modo de
  falha quando `data/derived/` esta ausente, degradado para travessao nos dois campos.
- Frescor tick-dirigido: apos devolver/fechar, o `opportunity_scores` publico so reflete o
  potencial decaido no proximo tick do agendador (ate ~60-80 s; um tick completo custa
  ~20 s, por isso NAO se recomputa sincronamente na acao). A saida/entrada da lista e
  imediata (dirigida por `status`). Aceitavel para o MVP e a registrar.
- Corrida sob READ COMMITTED entre a escrita interativa e o tick: mitigada pelo `UPDATE`
  guardado por `status='prospecting'` (0 linhas -> oportunidade indisponivel).
- Contagem do limite e verificada e a insercao ocorre na mesma transacao (fail-closed).

## Verificacao (ponta a ponta)

Pre-requisitos (como em R7M4): PostgreSQL provisionado e semeado (`db-setup`/seed) e os CSV
derivados em `data/derived/` para o modelo/relogio. Entao:

- Conducao ao vivo: subir `leadscorer/web:start`; via navegador (Claude-in-Chrome no

  Won/Lost/Devolver, e confirmar as invariantes com `verify.lisp` (ciclo aberto/fechado,

;;;; engagement.lisp --- Servicos interativos do ciclo de engajamento.
;;;;
;;;; As transicoes de estado que um agente dispara pela interface: engajar uma
;;;; oportunidade 'prospecting', fechar o ciclo com desfecho (won/lost) e devolver
;;;; sem desfecho. Complementam os servicos automaticos de 'cycle.lisp' (expiracao,
;;;; ranqueamento, decaimento) e honram as mesmas invariantes de persistencia
;;;; (migracao 0002 e 'verify.lisp'): o estado ativo casa 'status' com
;;;; 'engaged_by_id'/'engaged_at'; uma 'prospecting' nao tem ciclo aberto; um ciclo
;;;; fechado com desfecho tem valor de fechamento.
;;;;
;;;; CONTRATO DE TEMPO (ver o cabecalho de 'cycle.lisp'): os instantes 'engaged_at'
;;;; e 'closed_at' vivem na base de tempo VIRTUAL. O chamador passa NOW ja como
;;;; instante virtual, tipicamente '(current-virtual-now model)'; carimbar o tempo
;;;; de parede renderia idade negativa e uma oportunidade que nunca decai nem expira.
;;;;
;;;; Cada servico opera dentro de uma transacao unica e e fail-closed: o limite de
;;;; engajamentos e a disponibilidade da oportunidade sao verificados na mesma
;;;; transacao da escrita, de modo que uma corrida com o tick do agendador ou com
;;;; outro agente aborte a operacao em vez de violar uma invariante.

(in-package #:leadscorer)

;;; --- Condicoes ---

;;; A hierarquia de condicoes e o mecanismo padrao de sinalizacao de erro, nao um
;;; modelo de dados em CLOS: um tipo-base permite ao chamador tratar a familia toda,
;;; e cada subtipo carrega o dado que distingue a situacao para o diagnostico.

(define-condition engagement-error (error) ()
  (:documentation "Tipo-base das falhas dos servicos interativos de engajamento."))

(define-condition engagement-limit-reached (engagement-error)
  ((agent-id :initarg :agent-id :reader engagement-error-agent-id)
   (limit :initarg :limit :reader engagement-error-limit))
  (:report (lambda (condition stream)
             (format stream
                     "O agente ~A ja possui o limite de ~D oportunidades engajadas."
                     (engagement-error-agent-id condition)
                     (engagement-error-limit condition))))
  (:documentation "Sinalizada quando um agente no limite '*MAX-ENGAGEMENTS*' tenta
engajar outra oportunidade."))

(define-condition opportunity-not-available (engagement-error)
  ((opportunity-id :initarg :opportunity-id :reader engagement-error-opportunity-id))
  (:report (lambda (condition stream)
             (format stream
                     "A oportunidade ~A nao esta disponivel para a operacao solicitada."
                     (engagement-error-opportunity-id condition))))
  (:documentation "Sinalizada quando a oportunidade alvo nao esta no estado esperado,
tipicamente por ja ter sido engajada, devolvida ou expirada por outro ator."))

;;; --- Servicos ---

(defun count-agent-engagements (agent-id)
  "O numero de oportunidades atualmente engajadas (status 'engaging') pelo agente
AGENT-ID. Assume conexao ativa."
  (postmodern:query
   "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM opportunities
    WHERE status = 'engaging' AND engaged_by_id = $1"
   agent-id :single))

(defun engage-opportunity (opportunity-id agent-id now &key justification-id)
  "Engaja a oportunidade OPPORTUNITY-ID para o agente AGENT-ID no instante virtual
NOW, com a justificativa opcional JUSTIFICATION-ID (o id de 'engagement_justifications',
NIL dentro do top tier). Insere o ciclo aberto e transiciona a oportunidade para
'engaging', tudo em uma transacao. Assume conexao ativa. Retorna OPPORTUNITY-ID.
Sinaliza ENGAGEMENT-LIMIT-REACHED quando o agente ja atingiu '*MAX-ENGAGEMENTS*' e
OPPORTUNITY-NOT-AVAILABLE quando a oportunidade nao esta mais em 'prospecting'."
  (postmodern:with-transaction ()
    (when (>= (count-agent-engagements agent-id) *max-engagements*)
      (error 'engagement-limit-reached :agent-id agent-id :limit *max-engagements*))
    ;; A transicao e guardada por 'status = prospecting': afetar zero linhas
    ;; significa que outro ator ja engajou ou removeu a oportunidade (corrida com o
    ;; tick ou com outro agente), e a transacao aborta sem inserir o ciclo.
    (let ((affected
            (postmodern:execute
             "UPDATE opportunities
              SET status = 'engaging', engaged_by_id = $1, engaged_at = $2
              WHERE id = $3 AND status = 'prospecting'"
             agent-id now opportunity-id)))
      (when (zerop affected)
        (error 'opportunity-not-available :opportunity-id opportunity-id))
      (postmodern:execute
       "INSERT INTO engagements
            (opportunity_id, sales_agent_id, justification_id, engaged_at)
        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)"
       opportunity-id agent-id (sql-value justification-id) now)))
  opportunity-id)

(defun close-engagement (opportunity-id agent-id outcome now)
  "Fecha o ciclo aberto da oportunidade OPPORTUNITY-ID engajada por AGENT-ID com o
desfecho OUTCOME (:won ou :lost) no instante virtual NOW, e devolve a oportunidade a
'prospecting', em uma transacao. Assume conexao ativa. Retorna OPPORTUNITY-ID.
Sinaliza OPPORTUNITY-NOT-AVAILABLE quando nao ha ciclo aberto do agente para a
oportunidade.

Valor de fechamento: um 'won' registra o preco de tabela do produto, dado que o MVP
nao captura o valor negociado (simplificacao deliberada; o preco de tabela e um valor
de catalogo real, nao fabricado). Um 'lost' registra valor zero, na moeda da casa,
como faz a expiracao, satisfazendo a invariante de que um ciclo com desfecho tem
valor de fechamento."
  (check-type outcome (member :won :lost))
  (postmodern:with-transaction ()
    (let* ((price-row (postmodern:query
                       "SELECT p.list_price_amount, p.list_price_currency
                        FROM opportunities o
                        JOIN products p ON p.id = o.product_id
                        WHERE o.id = $1"
                       opportunity-id :row))
           (amount (ecase outcome
                     (:won (first price-row))
                     (:lost 0)))
           (currency (ecase outcome
                       (:won (second price-row))
                       (:lost *seed-currency*)))
           (outcome-string (ecase outcome (:won "won") (:lost "lost")))
           (affected
             (postmodern:execute
              "UPDATE engagements
               SET closed_at = $1, outcome = $2,
                   close_value_amount = $3, close_value_currency = $4
               WHERE opportunity_id = $5 AND sales_agent_id = $6
                 AND closed_at IS NULL"
              now outcome-string (sql-value amount) (sql-value currency)
              opportunity-id agent-id)))
      (when (zerop affected)
        (error 'opportunity-not-available :opportunity-id opportunity-id))
      (postmodern:execute
       "UPDATE opportunities
        SET status = 'prospecting', engaged_by_id = NULL, engaged_at = NULL
        WHERE id = $1"
       opportunity-id)))
  opportunity-id)

(defun return-engagement (opportunity-id agent-id now)
  "Devolve a oportunidade OPPORTUNITY-ID engajada por AGENT-ID a 'prospecting' sem
desfecho, fechando o ciclo aberto (grava 'closed_at' = NOW virtual, deixando
'outcome' nulo), em uma transacao. Assume conexao ativa. Retorna OPPORTUNITY-ID.
Sinaliza OPPORTUNITY-NOT-AVAILABLE quando nao ha ciclo aberto do agente para a
oportunidade. Fechar o ciclo preserva a invariante de que uma 'prospecting' nao tem
ciclo aberto; a ausencia de desfecho dispensa o valor de fechamento."
  (postmodern:with-transaction ()
    (let ((affected
            (postmodern:execute
             "UPDATE engagements SET closed_at = $1
              WHERE opportunity_id = $2 AND sales_agent_id = $3
                AND closed_at IS NULL"
             now opportunity-id agent-id)))
      (when (zerop affected)
        (error 'opportunity-not-available :opportunity-id opportunity-id))
      (postmodern:execute
       "UPDATE opportunities
        SET status = 'prospecting', engaged_by_id = NULL, engaged_at = NULL
        WHERE id = $1"
       opportunity-id)))
  opportunity-id)

;;;; engagement.lisp --- Testes Parachute dos servicos interativos de engajamento.

(in-package #:leadscorer/tests)

;;; --- Condicoes (puras) ---

(define-test engagement-conditions-carry-data
  (let ((limit (make-condition 'leadscorer:engagement-limit-reached
                               :agent-id 7 :limit 10))
        (unavailable (make-condition 'leadscorer:opportunity-not-available
                                     :opportunity-id 42)))
    (is = 7 (leadscorer:engagement-error-agent-id limit))
    (is = 10 (leadscorer:engagement-error-limit limit))
    (is = 42 (leadscorer:engagement-error-opportunity-id unavailable))
    ;; Ambas sao da familia ENGAGEMENT-ERROR, tratavel em bloco pelo chamador.
    (true (typep limit 'leadscorer:engagement-error))
    (true (typep unavailable 'leadscorer:engagement-error))))

;;; --- Servicos (integracao, gated por banco) ---

(defun open-cycle-of (opportunity-id)
  "A linha '(sales_agent_id engaged_at justification_id)' do ciclo aberto de
OPPORTUNITY-ID, ou NIL quando nao ha ciclo aberto."
  (postmodern:query
   "SELECT sales_agent_id, engaged_at, justification_id
    FROM engagements
    WHERE opportunity_id = $1 AND closed_at IS NULL"
   opportunity-id :row))

(defun integrity-violations ()
  "O total de violacoes das tres invariantes do estado ativo verificadas por
'verify.lisp': 'prospecting' com ciclo aberto, 'engaging' sem ciclo aberto e ciclo
fechado com desfecho sem valor. Assume conexao ativa."
  (postmodern:query
   "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM opportunities o
            WHERE o.status = 'prospecting'
              AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM engagements e
                          WHERE e.opportunity_id = o.id AND e.closed_at IS NULL))
         + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM opportunities o
            WHERE o.status = 'engaging'
              AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM engagements e
                              WHERE e.opportunity_id = o.id AND e.closed_at IS NULL))
         + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM engagements
            WHERE outcome IS NOT NULL AND close_value_amount IS NULL)"
   :single))

(define-test engage-service-integration
  (if (leadscorer::database-reachable-p)
      (leadscorer:with-database
        (leadscorer:run-migrations)
        (let* ((epoch leadscorer::*virtual-epoch*)
               (ids (leadscorer::setup-cycle-db epoch))
               (bob (getf ids :bob))
               (op-gtk (getf ids :op-gtk))
               (op-mg (getf ids :op-mg))
               (op-gtx (getf ids :op-gtx)))
          ;; Engajar uma 'prospecting' (op-gtk) por Bob, sem justificativa.
          (is = op-gtk (leadscorer:engage-opportunity op-gtk bob epoch))
          (is equal "engaging"
              (postmodern:query "SELECT status FROM opportunities WHERE id = $1"
                                op-gtk :single))
          (destructuring-bind (agent engaged-at justification) (open-cycle-of op-gtk)
            (is = bob agent)
            (is = epoch engaged-at)
            (is eq :null justification))
          ;; Engajar uma 'engaging' (op-gtx, ja de Ann) e recusado.
          (fail (leadscorer:engage-opportunity op-gtx bob epoch)
                'leadscorer:opportunity-not-available)
          ;; Justificativa registrada: engajar op-mg por Bob com um id de justificativa.
          (let ((just (postmodern:query
                       "INSERT INTO engagement_justifications (code, description)
                        VALUES ('direct-inquiry', 'x') RETURNING id" :single)))
            (leadscorer:engage-opportunity op-mg bob epoch :justification-id just)
            (is = just (third (open-cycle-of op-mg))))
          (is = 0 (integrity-violations))))
      (skip "PostgreSQL indisponivel; teste de engajamento ignorado.")))

(define-test engage-limit-integration
  (if (leadscorer::database-reachable-p)
      (leadscorer:with-database
        (leadscorer:run-migrations)
        (let* ((epoch leadscorer::*virtual-epoch*)
               (ids (leadscorer::setup-cycle-db epoch))
               (ann (getf ids :ann))
               (op-gtk (getf ids :op-gtk)))
          ;; Ann ja possui uma engajada (op-gtx no setup). Com o limite em 1, engajar
          ;; outra e recusado e nada e escrito (a op-gtk permanece 'prospecting').
          (let ((leadscorer::*max-engagements* 1))
            (fail (leadscorer:engage-opportunity op-gtk ann epoch)
                  'leadscorer:engagement-limit-reached))
          (is equal "prospecting"
              (postmodern:query "SELECT status FROM opportunities WHERE id = $1"
                                op-gtk :single))
          (is = 0 (integrity-violations))))
      (skip "PostgreSQL indisponivel; teste de limite ignorado.")))

(define-test close-and-return-integration
  (if (leadscorer::database-reachable-p)
      (leadscorer:with-database
        (leadscorer:run-migrations)
        (let ((epoch leadscorer::*virtual-epoch*))
          ;; Won: a op-gtx (engajada por Ann) fecha com o preco de tabela do GTX (550).
          (let* ((ids (leadscorer::setup-cycle-db epoch))
                 (ann (getf ids :ann))
                 (op-gtx (getf ids :op-gtx))
                 (op-gtk (getf ids :op-gtk))
                 (now (+ epoch leadscorer::+ms-per-day+)))
            (leadscorer:close-engagement op-gtx ann :won now)
            (is equal "prospecting"
                (postmodern:query "SELECT status FROM opportunities WHERE id = $1"
                                  op-gtx :single))
            (is = 1 (postmodern:query
                     "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM engagements
                      WHERE opportunity_id = $1 AND outcome = 'won'
                        AND closed_at = $2 AND close_value_amount = 550
                        AND close_value_currency = 'USD'"
                     op-gtx now :single))
            ;; Fechar uma oportunidade sem ciclo aberto (op-gtk 'prospecting') e recusado.
            (fail (leadscorer:close-engagement op-gtk ann :won now)
                  'leadscorer:opportunity-not-available)
            (is = 0 (integrity-violations)))
          ;; Lost: valor de fechamento zero.
          (let* ((ids (leadscorer::setup-cycle-db epoch))
                 (ann (getf ids :ann))
                 (op-gtx (getf ids :op-gtx))
                 (now (+ epoch leadscorer::+ms-per-day+)))
            (leadscorer:close-engagement op-gtx ann :lost now)
            (is = 1 (postmodern:query
                     "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM engagements
                      WHERE opportunity_id = $1 AND outcome = 'lost'
                        AND close_value_amount = 0"
                     op-gtx :single))
            (is = 0 (integrity-violations)))
          ;; Devolucao: ciclo fechado sem desfecho, oportunidade de volta a prospecting.
          (let* ((ids (leadscorer::setup-cycle-db epoch))
                 (ann (getf ids :ann))
                 (op-gtx (getf ids :op-gtx))
                 (now (+ epoch leadscorer::+ms-per-day+)))
            (leadscorer:return-engagement op-gtx ann now)
            (is equal "prospecting"
                (postmodern:query "SELECT status FROM opportunities WHERE id = $1"
                                  op-gtx :single))
            (is = 1 (postmodern:query
                     "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM engagements
                      WHERE opportunity_id = $1 AND closed_at = $2
                        AND outcome IS NULL"
                     op-gtx now :single))
            (is = 0 (integrity-violations)))))
      (skip "PostgreSQL indisponivel; teste de fechamento e devolucao ignorado.")))

(defun model-pair-context-index (model)
  "Uma hash-table de teste EQUAL, chaveada por (ACCOUNT . PRODUCT), cujo valor e a
plist '(:cadence-days D :last-close-value V)' com os campos de contexto do par vindos
do retrato estatico do MODEL. Expoe apenas dados de exibicao (nao as structs internas),
para enriquecer as linhas de oportunidade da camada de apresentacao. Um par ausente do
modelo simplesmente nao consta da tabela, e o chamador degrada os campos."
  (let ((table (make-hash-table :test #'equal)))
    (dolist (pair (model-pairs model) table)
      (setf (gethash (cons (pair-account pair) (pair-product pair)) table)
            (list :cadence-days (pair-cadence-days pair)
                  :last-close-value (pair-last-close-value pair))))))

;;;; apenas no retrato estatico do modelo de scoring: a cadencia de recompra (Prazo
;;;; de decisao) e o valor da ultima compra (Ultima compra), casando por (conta,
;;;; produto). O modelo e o do agendador quando em execucao, ou um carregado sob
;;;; demanda; quando indisponivel (CSV derivados ausentes), os dois campos degradam
;;;; para NIL e a apresentacao exibe um travessao. A funcao de enriquecimento e pura
;;;; e recebe o indice ja construido, de modo a ser testavel sem banco nem modelo.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

(defvar *web-model* nil
  "Modelo de scoring carregado sob demanda para a camada web, cacheado, quando o
agendador nao proveu um. Ver CURRENT-MODEL.")

(defun current-model ()
  "O modelo de scoring para a camada web: o do agendador ('*SCHEDULER-MODEL*') quando
em execucao, senao um carregado sob demanda e cacheado em '*WEB-MODEL*'. Retorna NIL
quando o modelo nao pode ser carregado (CSV derivados ausentes), caso em que os campos
dependentes do modelo degradam para NIL."
  (or *scheduler-model*
      *web-model*
      (setf *web-model*
            (handler-case (ls:load-model)
              (error (condition)
                (format *error-output*
                        "~&Modelo indisponivel para a camada web: ~A~%" condition)
                nil)))))

(defun enrich-rows-with-model (rows index)
  "Retorna ROWS, uma lista de plists de oportunidade, com as chaves ':cadence-days' e
':last-close-value' acrescentadas a partir de INDEX, a hash-table de
'ls:model-pair-context-index' chaveada por (conta . produto). Quando INDEX e NIL, ou o
par nao consta, os dois campos ficam NIL. Puro: nao consulta o banco nem o relogio."
  (mapcar (lambda (row)
            (let ((context (and index
                                (gethash (cons (getf row :account)
                                               (getf row :product))
                                         index))))
              (list* :cadence-days (getf context :cadence-days)
                     :last-close-value (getf context :last-close-value)
                     row)))
          rows))
